title: Keep the Windows WSL bridge out of Ninja codegen file dependencies
body: The native command cmake --build build/ninja --target recipe_simd_check --parallel 4 failed before running the check: ninja reported C:/Windows/System32/wsl.exe as a missing input for codegen/checks/recipe_simd_check.stamp, even though the WSL bridge was selected at configure. The pinned CodegenTool --recipe-simd-cpp --check invocation passed when run directly through the live queue after regenerating the output. Keep the bridge executable as a command dependency rather than a generated-file input, or publish its resolved path to Ninja as a valid external dependency.

title: Make generated VIXEN headers EOL-stable across Windows and WSL
body: Running the pinned recipe SIMD generator on the Windows checkout made RecipeSimd.g.hpp appear modified in git status while git diff was empty. git ls-files --eol reported i/lf w/mixed, and Git warned CRLF would be replaced by LF. The generator check passed after regeneration, but I had to git restore the exact generated file to normalize it back to w/lf and keep the lane clean. Make the emitter write the repository's canonical LF output on Windows so a fresh check does not leave platform-only worktree drift.

title: Check the Linux Vulkan SDK glslang include path without a false fatal diagnostic
body: A fresh CMake preset vixen-wsl configure with the auto-provisioned LunarG SDK 1.4.350.1 printed the diagnostic Fatal Error: glslang directory not found for <sdk>/x86_64/Include/glslang, although the official Linux SDK has the headers under <sdk>/x86_64/include/glslang. Configure continued and the Dozen target built. Check the Linux case-correct include path and reserve fatal wording for a real configure stop, so a usable SDK does not require manual source inspection.
